questions.question: Your recommendation agent is stuck suggesting similar items. What technique might help?
questions.explanation: An epsilon-greedy exploration strategy helps a recommendation agent avoid repeatedly suggesting similar items. Most of the time, the agent exploits the option currently estimated to be best, but with a small probability represented by epsilon, the agent explores a different option. This balance between exploration and exploitation helps the agent discover potentially better recommendations. Reducing the dataset, removing the reward function, or using a smaller model does not directly address insufficient exploration.

questions.question: What is overfitting in machine learning?

options.text: When a model performs well on training data but poorly on new data
When a model is too simple

questions.explanation: Overfitting occurs when a machine learning model learns the training data too specifically instead of learning patterns that generalize to unseen examples. An overfit model typically achieves very good performance on its training dataset but substantially worse performance on validation or test data. A model that is too simple is more commonly associated with underfitting. Although limited data can contribute to overfitting, insufficient data itself is not the definition of overfitting.

questions.question: Your application needs to process thousands of independent prompts asynchronously, where immediate responses are unnecessary. Which feature may be appropriate?

options.text: A separate synchronous request for every prompt with a long timeout

questions.explanation: The Message Batches API is designed for asynchronous processing of groups of Messages API requests. It can suit workloads that tolerate delayed results; check current availability, limits, and processing guarantees in the docs.
